context: Field extensions: algebraic extension that is an algebraically closed field

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: Given a field F, an algebraic closure of F is an extension field K containing F in which every element is algebraic over F and every nonconstant polynomial over K has a root in K.

context: Field theory: no nontrivial algebraic field extensions

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: A field K is algebraically closed precisely when it has no proper algebraic field extension; equivalently, each nonconstant one-variable polynomial with coefficients in K admits a root in K.

formulations.equivalence_note: Equivalent polynomial-root characterization to the no-proper-algebraic-extension formulation (Stacks Lemma 9.10.2).
formulations.text: A field F is algebraically closed exactly when every polynomial in F[x] of positive degree has at least one zero in F.

context: Topology: basis consisting of open sets

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: For a topological space X, a basis is a family B of open sets such that, whenever an open U contains x, some member of B contains x and is itself contained in U.

context: Topology: subbasis whose finite intersections are a basis

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: A subbasis for an existing topology on X is a family of open subsets whose finite intersections form a basis for that topology, with the empty intersection taken as X.

context: Algebraic geometry: spectrum as a locally ringed space

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring equipped with its structure sheaf.

context: Category theory: universal outgoing morphism

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: In a category C, an object I is initial if every object Y of C is the target of exactly one morphism originating at I.

context: Category theory: universal incoming morphism

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: In a category C, an object T is terminal (final) if for every object Y of C there is exactly one morphism from Y to T.

context: Set theory: initial ordinal of a well-orderable set

formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.
formulations.text: For a set A, its cardinality may be represented by the smallest ordinal equipotent to A, meaning the least ordinal for which a bijection with A exists.

context: Field theory: monic irreducible polynomial of an algebraic element

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: If an element alpha of an extension E/k is algebraic over k, its minimal polynomial over k is the unique monic polynomial generating the kernel of evaluation k[t] to E at alpha; it is irreducible over k.

context: Field theory: minimal root-containing extension of a polynomial

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.

context: Topology: descending chain condition on closed subsets

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A topological space is Noetherian when every descending sequence of its closed subsets eventually becomes constant.

context: Topology: open-cover compactness without Hausdorffness

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A topological space X is quasi-compact if each open cover of X contains a finite subcollection that still covers X; no Hausdorff condition is required.

context: Topology: inverse images of quasi-compact open sets

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A continuous map f:X to Y is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.

context: Commutative algebra: Zariski topology on prime ideals

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For a commutative ring R, the prime spectrum Spec(R) is the set consisting of all prime ideals of R, equipped with the Zariski topology whose closed sets comprise the common zero-locus sets V(I).

context: Category theory: simultaneous left and right exactness

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A functor between categories with the requisite finite limits and colimits is exact if it preserves both finite limits and finite colimits (equivalently it is both left exact and right exact).

context: Field theory: finite vector-space degree

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A field extension E/F has degree equal to the vector-space dimension of E over F; the extension is finite exactly when this dimension is a finite integer.

context: Category theory: left/right adjunction via natural Hom-set bijections

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For functors L:C to D and R:D to C, L is left adjoint to R when there are bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C, natural in both X and Y.

context: Algebra: graded free associative algebra generated by a module

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For an R-module M, its tensor algebra is the graded associative R-algebra obtained by taking the direct sum over n at least zero of the n-fold tensor powers of M, with the degree-zero summand R and multiplication by concatenation of tensors.

context: Commutative algebra: integrally closed domain

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: An integral domain R is normal when every element of its fraction field that satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in R already belongs to R.

context: Commutative algebra: normality of all prime localizations

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A commutative ring R is normal if each localization R_p at a prime ideal p is an integrally closed domain in its own fraction field.

context: Commutative algebra: prime annihilator of an element
display_term: Associated prime ideal of a module

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is associated to M if p is the annihilator ideal of some element of M.

context: Field theory: purely inseparable algebraicity in positive characteristic

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For a field F of characteristic p greater than zero, an extension K/F is purely inseparable if, for every alpha in K, some p-power alpha^(p^n) lies in F. The trivial extension is also purely inseparable in any characteristic.

context: Algebraic geometry: a closed immersion into an open subscheme

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A morphism of schemes is a locally closed immersion if it admits a factorization through a closed immersion followed by an open immersion.

context: Field theory: extensions generated by roots of X^p-X-a

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For a field K of prime characteristic p, an Artin-Schreier extension is obtained by adjoining a solution of t^p - t = a, for a in K; a nontrivial such extension has cyclic Galois group of order p.

context: Algebraic geometry: sheaf of rings with local stalks

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A locally ringed space is a topological space X together with a sheaf of rings O_X whose stalk at every point of X is a local ring.

context: Algebraic geometry: locally ringed morphism with local homomorphisms on stalks

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A morphism of locally ringed spaces consists of a continuous map and a compatible morphism of structure sheaves, with induced maps on all stalks required to be local ring homomorphisms.

context: Commutative algebra: finite presentation of finitely generated ideals

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A ring R is coherent if every finitely generated ideal of R admits a finite presentation as an R-module.

context: Field theory: one generator of a finite field extension
display_term: Primitive element of a field extension

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: For a finite field extension E/F, a primitive element is an element alpha of E such that the smallest subfield containing F and alpha is all of E.

context: Field theory: tensor-product injectivity under chosen embeddings

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: If fields K and L extend k inside a common field, K and L are linearly disjoint over k when the multiplication map from their tensor product over k to their compositum KL is injective.

context: Category theory: colimit of a span

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: Given morphisms B to A and B to C in a category, a pushout is an object P equipped with morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B, such that every other compatible pair of maps to an object T factors uniquely through P.

context: Algebraic geometry: left-cancellative morphism in the category of schemes

formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.
formulations.text: A morphism f:X to Y of schemes is a monomorphism when for every scheme T and two morphisms g,h:T to X, equality f composed with g = f composed with h forces g=h.
